title: First halt in a padded run
statement: Let $M$ be a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine, let $x$ be a finite binary input, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$. If $c$ is not halted and the run from $c$ is halted after $t$ steps, then there is a time $u$ with $0<u\le t$ such that the run is not halted at any time $v<u$, and the configuration at time $u$ equals the configuration at time $t$.
hypotheses_covered: $k$ is a natural number of work tapes
$M$ is a multi-tape Turing machine with Boolean symbols and state set $S$
$x$ is a finite list of Boolean input symbols
the configuration after $t$ steps is halted
replaced:
Let a multi-tape machine, started in a live configuration, be halted after $t$
steps. Then there is a positive time $u \le t$ such that the machine is not
halted at any earlier time, and the $u$-step run equals the $t$-step run in
every field: a padded halting run can be cut at its first halt without changing
any endpoint.
